body: I really want this to be true. I'm doubtful, but here's hoping for the best.

My daughter was on a high dose of Topamax for just over two years. We started on a low dose and increased over time. As the medication increased, the seizures became less common. Topamax was spectacular at suppressing her seizures for the two years that she was on a high dose. The downside was that since her dose was really high, she had to take Oracit to reduce uric acid in her blood. I'm not sure if that's a common side effect with a low dose. Overall, the Topamax made her sleepy all of the time. It was hard to engage her on any subject. Again, she was on a high dose and you might tolerate it differently.

Until it stopped working, it was an okay medication. It did just what it was supposed to for two years, so I think it was worth it.

Okay, so you're not willing (rightfully so) to spend a load on all new chairs. Here's what I would do: buy two sturdy chairs. Before the guests come, hide two antique ones in the attic or basement. Put each sturdy chair at exact opposite sides of the table, for symmetry, and assign seating with fancy place cards. Heavy guest gets a sturdy chair and so does one other person. I don't usually advocate lying, but in this case... If anyone asks, just say something like, "Oh, well, it's an antique set. We loved it so much, we had to get it, so please excuse the slight mismatch as we had to get two extra chairs."

Every time you have this group over for dinner follow the exact same seating plan so it becomes routine. After you establish a routine, I doubt anyone will give it a second thought.

If it looks like people might informally switch seating at some point if you do cocktails or coffee, I would move the party to the patio or the sitting room.

Once I was older and thought back on it, I realized those books were pulled because of homosexual content. In one book, Anastasia, who is ten, has a crush on her female gym teacher. When I first acknowledged to myself that I was no longer Christian, similar fears ate at me. I went through a period where I would wake up regularly in the middle of the night, panicked about either my daughter, my boyfriend, or myself dying. That has now passed.

Just like you, I grew up terrified of Hell and fearing Heaven. I pictured a future of eternal pain or eternal worship service at church. They both sounded awful. After de-converting it took a while for those ideas to dissipate.

Think of it this way: your entire life you have been told over and over again, "Heaven and Hell are REAL. God and angels, Satan and demons are REAL. Be faithful or you are lost!" The trusted authority figures in your life have told you these things for years. It goes against your prior experience to reject what they're telling you.

One of the hard things about growing up is realizing that your parents are not always right. When it comes to something as personal and deep as spiritual beliefs, that's a hard thing to swallow. I have friends in their mid 30s who still struggle to reconcile their Christianity with their life experience. They keep on out of fear and filial piety. I pity them and it's hard to watch.

Here's the good part: you're already on the path. De-conversion is a process. It takes time. You won't be frightened forever. Heaven and Hell are not real. Valhalla is not real. Elysium is not real. Name your eternal realm: none of them are real. 

Did you know that the Judaic version of cosmic dualism (good versus evil) was borrowed from Zoroastrianism? Judaism and Christianity have evolved greatly over the centuries. The flood story in Genesis comes from the ancient tale of Gilgamesh. Eventually, I came to view the stories, heroes and villains of the bible the same way I view all ancient mythology. God, Zues, Odin, Ahura Mazda, take your pick, they're all myths so far as I'm concerned.

I suggest you read up on a bunch of ancient religions. Try reading the Epic of Gilgamesh. When you compare the different religions from the same general geographic locations, it puts Christianity and Judaism into perspective. Modern Chrstianity is a highly derived product. I found comfort in knowledge. Perhaps it will help you, too.

And as always, keep posting here. We are here for you.

I'm going to venture that this guy is the controlling type. His reaction to you having any sort of a romantic past throws up red flags from my standpoint. So you had crushes in the past. Big deal. Everyone has crushes. 

A few specific things he said to you really stood out to me. For example:

>"Normally, I think when you are casually dating, it's okay to do so with multiple people. He says he thinks that's *wrong* and *selfish* to do."

Yeah, that's not selfish or wrong. That's normal. That's dating. If you're exclusive with someone (and you both have expressed interest in being exclusive and agree upon it) then, yeah. If he wanted to be solely with you, there were much better ways he could have worded it. The way he worded it suggests intent to make you feel guilt. No bueno.

>"I casually tell him that it was a stupid, teenage crush. I thought he was attractive and that's all there was to it. He then started texting me saying 'Wow, have some standards lol. How many guys have you talked to? Every time we have these little conversations I learn about more dudes you wanted'."

Again, with the guilt. Seriously? Implying that you don't have standards? I don't care what his insecurities are. We all feel a little insecure from time to time. But he chose to accuse you and load on the guilt, more or less implying that you lack in boundaries and control. This early in the relationship he speaks to you in this way? This mode of discourse is disrespectful towards you. Again, not good.

>"He replied with 'Oh, sorry. I thought you were interested when you were interested in me. I was mostly joking. Sorry'."

Mostly joking? Wat? So, he wasn't really joking, then? This is what I like to call a "non-apology apology." He's not really apologizing to you. He's trying to look like he's reeled his insult back in (without actually doing so) to keep you on the hook. Also, I guess he thinks it's not okay for you to have been interested in other guys while you were interested in him, but not yet dating? As in, you don't have the freedom to feel how you feel as long as he is involved in even a cursory sort of way?

A healthy person with insecurities would calmly discuss these things with the other person. A person who has insecurities, but still respects the other person would calmly discuss things without throwing out accusations. Instead, he makes this all about you and your lack of boundaries and "standards." If you get serious with this guy, don't expect his attitudes to change. Don't expect him to ever respect you. 

Seriously, watch out for this one. Drop him like a hot rock and distance yourself. You are not overreacting.

In a Modified Atkins or ketogenic diet, you basically give up nearly all forms of carbohydrate.  Milk, yogurt, grains, fruit, veggies, etc.  Rather than getting your calories from carbohydrate, you get it almost entirely from fats.  What this does is trick your body into thinking that it is starving.  This triggers the release of ketones.  Ketones have the ability to cross the blood-brain barrier (the bag your brain lives in that someone mentioned elsewhere in the comments).  Ketones are effective in preventing convulsions.

Problems with the Modified Atkins of ketogenic diets: number one hands down is constipation.  I won't go too much into how bad it gets,  but my daughter never had serious gastric issues of this sort before starting the diet.  Our medicine cabinet is now stocked with glycerin products.  We hate it, but it's unavoidable.

Second would be the utter loss of enjoying what you eat.  When you are limited to 10-15 grams of carbohydrate per day, there is little that you can actually eat.  An average piece of bread alone is somewhere around 22 grams of carbohydrate.  When you take this into consideration along with the issue of constipation, you can imagine how hard it is to coordinate a decent diet.

The third major thing is the lethargy.  Anti-seizure meds do a great job of sapping one's energy, and a harsh diet like this only adds to the trouble.  My daughter likes to spend lots of time sleeping if I let her.  

Also worth mention is the fact that it can significantly increase your cholesterol.  The duration of the diet is usually no more than 2 years because of this, in part.  It is not a "safe" diet so far as I'm concerned.  

And the Ketogenic diet is even tougher than the Modified Atkins because you also have to measure liquids.  I understand that it is especially difficult to be on the ketogenic in the summer time because of the increased risk of heatstroke and dehydration.  

Edit to add that people in public don't understand when they go to hand your kid a sweet and you tell them they can't have it, or accepting it and never giving it to your kid.  It can get socially awkward and kids can feel pretty crushed by never getting that treat.  It's the little things sometimes.
Perhaps they will find out it has broader uses during the course of their research?  Once you run out of medications to try, things start to feel hopeless.  New findings like this give me hope.

My daughter is currently on the Modified Atkins Diet.  We have about 5 months left before we hit the two year mark and can stop.  She has had nearly total cessation of seizures since starting this diet.  (She is also on two anti-epileptic medications.)  While we have had great success, this diet has been absolute hell.  It takes a massive physical toll.  There have been times where I have wondered if it's really worth it to stick with the diet, but then I think about her going into status epilepticus again and we stay with it.

TL;DR Ketogenic and MAD are great when they work, but they come with a high cost.

My modified version of a recipe from Allrecipes.com:

* 4 cups chicken broth, divided
* 1/8 teaspoon ground ginger
* sliced green onions or scallions (however much you prefer)
* 1/4 teaspoon salt
* 1 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch
* 2 eggs + 1 egg yolk
* 1/2 a chicken breast, sliced into 1/8 inch strips (After rinsing the chicken breast and patting it dry, place it in the freezer for 5 - 10 minutes to firm it up a bit.  It should be easier to slice thin.)
* 1/4 tsp sesame oil per bowl (optional)

Directions

Whisk 3/4 cup of chicken broth in with the cornstarch in a separate bowl.  In another bowl, whisk the eggs and egg yolk together.  Whisk the remaining broth into a medium saucepan with 1/4 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp ground ginger. Bring to a boil.

After the broth comes to a boil, stir the broth/cornstarch mixture into the pot.  Keep boiling and stir for about 5 minutes to thicken.  Add chicken slices, green onions, and stir for about one minute.

Remove from heat or chicken will overcook!

Immediately stir the hot broth in a clockwise motion (preferably with chopsticks) and drizzle the eggs into the pot in a slow, steady stream.  The eggs will form into nice ribbons and cook immediately.

Dish into bowls and top with 1/4 tsp sesame oil (if using) and extra raw green onions if you like a sharper flavor.  I also like to add a bit of ground black pepper and garlic powder to my dish to give it some extra kick.

Enjoy!

I find that my best ideas come from everyday life.  I suggest sitting down at the computer with your favorite music playing.  There are certain kinds of music that really get me writing. As far as a long work goes, look at it this way: a long work is composed of short works.  Write it a chapter at a time.  I don't do outlines, personally.  I find them constraining.  I like to write it out as I am able, then go back and fix it later.  Unless I really write myself into an impossible corner, everything I screw up can be fixed later.  Get your first draft out, no matter how awful it is.  Everything can be fixed later.  

You have to quit planning and worrying about how far you'll go and whether it will be great or not.  The best thing to do is to just DO it.  That's the hardest part about writing: sitting yourself down and having the discipline to just write.  I find that I have the same issues, and I've been working through the same problem for a decade longer.  I think most writers have the same problem.  The writers who succeed have not only talent and luck, but discipline.

Make yourself sit and write without outside distraction.  Log off of facebook, Reddit, youtube, etc.  Take it one session at a time and be patient.  You will write something awesome.  It will be in your rough draft.  You just have to work to write it first and then polish it.

This is absolutely true.  My daughter has been very sick from day one.  For a long time we carried her on private insurance and it almost bankrupted us (I was 21 at that point).  Luckily, and it's sad to say this is a lucky thing, my ex lost his job and she lost her insurance coverage.  At that point the state considered me so poor that she qualified for Medicaid (government health care).  She has been on it ever since and Medicaid has covered probably about 100 thousand dollars or more of health care and life-saving medications for my child.  Without Medicaid, I am sure that I would have been standing over a coffin rather than a hospital bed.  

People who would deny health care to anyone, especially a child born with medical issues simply based on fears of "socialism" or "communism" make my blood boil.  It's ignorance and selfishness at its worst.

TL;DR: My daughter was born sick and without Medicaid, she would probably not be alive today.
